title: Grateful Dead Live at Palace Theater on 1972-09-24
lineage: SBD> MR> CASS> DAT> CDR> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a blistering September ’72 Palace show – crystal‑clear enough to hear the thunderous Phil bass, with a monster 30‑minute Dark Star, soaring Bird Song and fiery Playin'.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently praised for its high energy, especially the epic Dark Star/China Cat/S Rider sequence, plus standout moments from Cumberland Blues, Sugaree, Friend of the Devil and the Great>Bertha>Promised combo. Recording quality is generally good – a clean soundboard source with only minor vocal muddiness, occasional cuts and brief tuning quirks that don’t detract from the overall experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen reviews overwhelmingly praise the musical performance (many 5‑star comments) while noting only modest recording flaws; the weighting yields a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard mix with occasional vocal muddiness, brief cuts (e.g., in I Know You Rider) and minor tuning slips; overall listenable and detailed.

standout_songs: Dark Star > China Cat Sunflower > The Other One (Rider)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set builds with strong blues‑rock numbers and tight solos, while the second set launches into a monumental Dark Star that segues seamlessly into China Cat and a powerful Rider, keeping the momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for perfect tone, soaring solos, and leading the jams (especially during Dark Star).
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as booming, with bass that shook apartments; many reviewers call his playing a tour‑de‑force.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for clear, bell‑like comping and strong solo on I Know You Rider.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted for tasteful electric piano fills during Dark Star and solid work on Promised Land.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers (Bill/Mickey) receive praise for crisp, tight playing that drives the jams; no major complaints.
